explanations: terra: One who purchases magic is said to have no خَلَاقٍ in the Hereafter, another concrete use of the named root's “good share” sense as something forfeited.

luna: The section labels خَلاق, from root خ ل ق, as a share of good fortune; this verse says the person seeking only worldly life has no خلاق in the Hereafter, setting a boundary against the lasting share promised to believers. | terra: The person who asks only for this world has no خَلَاقٍ in the Hereafter, the named derivative's explicit picture of an absent good share opposite the uncut wage.
terra: Between the worldly-only request in 2:200 and the earned share in 2:202, these speakers ask for good in both this world and the Hereafter, completing the section's two domains of recompense.
terra: Those who ask for good in both worlds have a share of what they earned, completing the contrast begun in 2:200 with a returned portion tied to acquisition.

luna: The section defines أجر as the return for a good act; in the same charity passage as 2:262-64, 2:261 pictures spending for God multiplying like grain with seven ears, making abundance a concrete form of returned reward. | terra: The expenditure passage begins with a seed multiplying to seven hundred and beyond, so the reward beside 2:262's ban on reproach grows rather than diminishes.

luna: The section's B003 dictionary sense of م ن ن is a favor made heavy by claiming it; this verse says spenders do not follow what they gave with منّ or harm, and places their reward with their Lord. | terra: The verse joins both key nouns: those who do not follow expenditure with مَنّ or hurt have أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ, a reward free of the giver's reproach.

luna: The section's secondary sense of م ن ن includes harm attached to a gift; 2:263 says kind speech and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury, clarifying that the recipient's treatment matters alongside the act. | terra: A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by harm, extending 2:262-264 by distinguishing a gift that leaves no wound or oppressive reminder.

luna: The section's B003 sense of م ن ن as reproachful favor appears in the command not to cancel charity with المن والأذى; the washed bare stone pictures a good act emptied by that treatment. | terra: The command not to nullify charity by الْمَنِّ وَالْأَذَى makes human reproach a cause that destroys an otherwise good deed, illuminating the opposite force of God's unburdening reward.

luna: After 2:264's charity erased by reproach, this verse depicts spending for God's approval as a garden that yields twice its produce; its own image supplies the fruitful counterpart to giving that is emptied. | terra: After the nullified charity of 2:264, sincere expenditure is a high garden whose yield doubles and still receives dew, picturing an act whose return is preserved and increased.

luna: The section reads a reward free of minnah as one that does not burden its recipient; this verse says spending is for God's face and will be repaid fully without wrong, joining unclaimed giving to complete recompense.
terra: Those who spend by night and day, secretly and openly, have their reward with their Lord and no fear or grief, extending the same expenditure-and-reward sequence beyond reproach.
terra: Every soul is paid in full for what it earned and no one is wronged, a general judgment-day formulation of unreduced return.
terra: Believers who do righteous deeds are paid their wages in full, a direct formula of recompense without reduction.
terra: Those who trade God's covenant and their oaths for a small price have no خَلَاقَ in the Hereafter; a short worldly payment displaces the lasting share.
terra: Against the source dictionary's image of a snapped rope, believers are commanded to hold fast together to حَبْلِ اللَّهِ; the held rope supplies a concrete opposite of severed continuity.
terra: Repentant, steadfast doers receive forgiveness and Gardens in which they remain, followed by the judgment that this is an excellent reward for workers.
terra: The ayah distinguishes one who desires the reward of this world from one who desires the reward of the Hereafter, making the two domains of returned recompense explicit.
terra: God gives the faithful both the reward of this world and the beautiful reward of the Hereafter, directly realizing the section's twofold definition of ecr.
terra: God's sending of a messenger is called a favor conferred upon the believers; the positive divine subject distinguishes this menn from a human reminder that burdens its recipient.

luna: The section says death can cut a life but not the believer's promised wage; this verse says those killed in God's way are alive with their Lord and provided for, making death no endpoint for their provision. | terra: Those killed in God's path are alive with their Lord and provided for, supplying the post-death scene behind 3:171's assurance that believers' reward is not lost.
luna: Continuing the martyrs' scene in 3:169, this verse shows them rejoicing in God's bounty and without fear for those not yet joined them, giving the post-death provision a continuing horizon.

luna: This verse completes the martyrs' sequence with glad tidings of bounty and the statement that God does not waste the believers' reward, directly answering the section's concern that death end a wage. | terra: The martyrs rejoice that God does not waste the reward of believers, preserving recompense beyond their deaths.
terra: Every soul tastes death, yet wages are paid in full on Resurrection Day; death ends the earthly run without cutting off the recompense.

luna: The section promises a wage that is not diminished; amid migration, hardship, fighting, and death, this verse says God will not let any worker's work be lost, tying costly actions to preserved recompense. | terra: God answers that He never lets the work of any worker, male or female, be lost, directly securing intentional action against disappearance.

luna: The section glosses غير ممنون as neither cut nor diminished; this verse says God does not wrong an atom's weight, and multiplies a good deed, adding full justice and increase to that promise. | terra: God does not wrong even an atom's weight; He multiplies a good deed and grants a great reward, replacing possible diminution with increase.
terra: People are reminded that God conferred favor on them after they once stood in the same condition as those they now confront, making divine menn a transforming mercy rather than a boast.
terra: One who leaves home migrating to God and His messenger, then is overtaken by death, already has his reward incumbent on God; death cuts the journey but not its intended work's return.
terra: Any believing man or woman who does righteous deeds enters the Garden and is not wronged even by a tiny amount, matching both the condition and the unreduced result.

luna: The section's dictionary definition of أجر allows recompense in this life or the next; 4:134 states that both kinds of reward are with God, making that twofold scope explicit. | terra: Whoever wants worldly reward is reminded that with God are the rewards of both this world and the Hereafter, holding both returns under one divine source.
terra: Those who believe in God and all His messengers are promised their wages, with forgiveness and mercy locating the payment in divine grace.
terra: Believers who do righteous deeds are paid their wages in full and receive an increase from divine bounty.
terra: The challengers ask whether these are the people God favored among them; the ayah identifies gratitude, rather than indebted humiliation, as the fitting response to divine menn.
terra: The Prophet follows earlier guidance and tells his hearers that he asks no wage for it; revelation is offered as a reminder rather than a reproachful favor.
terra: A person who brings a good deed receives ten like it and no one is wronged, making the earned return enlarged rather than reduced.
terra: Those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer are assured that God does not waste the reward of those who set things right.
terra: The addressed people consume their خَلَاق as earlier peoples consumed theirs and plunge into the same vain talk; an allotted share used up in the nearer life reverses the enduring good share.

luna: The section's B001 dictionary sense of م ن ن includes fatigue that stops a traveler; here traveler's نصب in God's cause is recorded as a good deed, and God does not waste the reward of those who do good. | terra: Thirst, fatigue, hunger, each step, and every gain against an enemy are written as righteous work because God does not waste the reward of those who do good; even weariness cannot sever the return.

luna: The section defines recompense as what comes back for an act; continuing 9:120's journey scene, this verse records each small or large expenditure and each valley crossed so God can repay the best of their deeds. | terra: Every small or great expenditure and every traversed valley is recorded so that God may reward them by the best they did, making no intentional effort disappear from the return.

luna: The section's B003 dictionary note on حسن connects doing good with the best and more as reward; this verse says those who do good have al-husna and ziyada, extending the reward beyond the deed's return. | terra: Those who do good receive الْحُسْنَىٰ وَزِيَادَةٌ and are people of the Garden; this is the section's named حسن formulation in which beautiful action returns as the most beautiful outcome plus increase.
terra: Noah asks no wage from his people and places his reward only upon God, separating prophetic work from a favor held over its recipients.
terra: Creation of the heavens and earth is made a test of who is best in deed, another direct movement of حسن from creation into intentional work.
terra: Patient people who do righteous deeds form the exception to the preceding human swings of despair and boastfulness, and they receive forgiveness and a great reward.
terra: Those who intend worldly life and its adornment are paid their works in full within it and are not shortchanged there, demonstrating the dictionary claim that a work's return can be worldly.
terra: The people fully paid in 11:15 have only Fire in the Hereafter and their deeds there collapse, marking the boundary between a finite worldly return and the uncut otherworldly wage.
terra: Noah says he asks his people for no wealth because his wage is only with God, a concrete stance of service without human repayment.
terra: Hud asks no wage from his people; his reward belongs to the One who originated him, tying creation to a recompense that does not burden the addressee.

luna: The section's “not cut off” reward is restated for the blessed as عطاء غير مجذوذ, a gift that is not severed; the different wording confirms the same continuity. | terra: The people made happy receive عَطَاءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ, an unsevered gift stated with a different cutting word and therefore a direct semantic counterpart to غير ممنون.
terra: The command to be patient is grounded in the assurance that God does not waste the reward of those who do good.
terra: Joseph's worldly establishment is followed by the rule that God does not waste the reward of those who do good, displaying a return already given within earthly life.
terra: After Joseph's earthly return in 12:56, this ayah states that the reward of the Hereafter is better for believing, mindful people.

luna: The section notes م ن ن can name a benign favor as well as a burdensome one; Yusuf says مَنَّ الله علينا, then says God does not waste the reward of those who do good, joining divine favor to returned recompense. | terra: Joseph says قَدْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا and immediately affirms that God does not waste the reward of those who do good; gracious divine menn and preserved recompense meet in one ayah.
terra: Joseph's story is a reminder to the worlds for which the Prophet asks no wage, so its hearers are not made debtors to him.
terra: The promised Garden has food and shade that are دائم, a concrete image of provision whose supply and shelter do not run out.
terra: The messengers say that God bestows favor on whomever He wills among His servants, a direct positive use of the named root with God as giver.

luna: The section says fatigue can sever a walk; in the Garden described here no نصب touches its people and they are not expelled, joining freedom from weariness to remaining there. | terra: The Garden's people are touched by no fatigue and are never expelled from it, combining the negation of exhaustion with uninterrupted possession.
terra: Those who migrate after being wronged receive a good settlement in this world, while the reward of the Hereafter is greater, another explicit two-domain return.
luna: This verse describes people being taken in death or returned to أرذل العمر until knowledge fades, a concrete bodily decline that illuminates the section's descending human condition.

luna: The section contrasts a life that ends with a reward not cut off; this verse says what people possess will perish while what is with God remains, then promises patient people their reward. | terra: What people possess runs out while what is with God remains, and the patient are recompensed by the best of their deeds; this directly explains how a returned wage can stand outside life's dwindling line.

luna: The section connects أجر to the return for work and حسن to what is best; this verse promises people who do good their reward بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون. | terra: Believing men and women who act righteously receive a good life and a reward according to بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ, joining faith, work, wage, and “best.”
terra: On the day each soul pleads for itself, everyone is paid in full for what they did and is not wronged.
terra: Whoever intends the Hereafter, strives for it with its due striving, and is a believer finds that striving appreciated; intention, work, faith, and returned recognition coincide.
terra: The Book gives believers who do righteous deeds good news of أَجْرًا حَسَنًا, joining the section's work, wage, and حسن vocabulary.
terra: The recipients of the good reward in 18:2 remain in it forever, explicitly supplying the duration implied by “uncut.”
terra: Earth's adornment is a test of which people are best in deed, using the same أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا formulation that the section connects to recompense.

luna: The section connects أجر with good action and notes the root حسن in “best”; this verse says God does not waste the reward of one who أحسن عملا, directly joining recompense to excellent work. | terra: God says He does not waste the reward of whoever أَحْسَنَ عَمَلًا, explicitly moving حسن into intentional work and its preserved wage.
terra: The good workers whose reward is not wasted in 18:30 receive lasting Gardens and ornaments, and the ayah calls this an excellent reward and resting place.
terra: Worldly wealth and children are adornment, while enduring righteous deeds are better with the Lord in reward and hope; passing possession, lasting work, and recompense meet explicitly.
terra: The record omits neither small nor great deeds, people find what they did present, and the Lord wrongs no one; work is preserved whole for its return.
terra: Moses' companion says they have met weariness from their journey; the scene concretizes the section's dictionary explanation of fatigue stopping a traveler on the road.
terra: The question announces the greatest losers in works, opening a precise reversal of the section's preserved wage.
terra: Their striving goes astray in worldly life while they think they are doing beautiful work, exposing mistaken أَحْسَنَ صُنْعًا as the opposite of rewarded righteous action.
terra: Because they deny God's signs and the meeting with Him, their works collapse and receive no weight at resurrection, a direct reversal of an unreduced wage.
terra: Believers who do righteous deeds receive the Gardens of Paradise as hospitality, restating the section's condition with its otherworldly return.
terra: They remain there and seek no transfer away from it, making the reward in 18:107 stable and uninterrupted.
terra: God increases the guided in guidance, and enduring righteous deeds are better with the Lord in reward and final return, directly pairing lasting action with lasting recompense.
terra: God tells Moses that He had already conferred favor on him another time, locating menn in a history of rescue and care rather than reproach.
terra: Whoever comes to God as a believer having done righteous deeds receives the highest ranks, reversing the downward line through the same faith-and-work condition.
terra: Those high ranks are Gardens beneath which rivers flow, with the recipients remaining there, supplying the unbroken duration of 20:75's reward.
terra: Whoever performs righteous deeds as a believer fears neither injustice nor هَضْمًا, an explicit assurance that the return will not be diminished.
terra: No human before the Prophet was granted earthly immortality, and his possible death will not make his opponents immortal; this sets the boundary between a mortal messenger and his uncut wage.
terra: For one who does righteous deeds while believing, there is no denial of the striving and it is written down, directly opposing a work whose return is lost or cut.

luna: The section describes a downward human line ending with life's exhaustion; this verse stages human development through old age, when some are returned to أرذل العمر, and places that decline beside resurrection.
terra: The source dictionary explains memnūn through a rope being cut; this ayah literally stages extending a rope and then cutting it, though its own context concerns rage at divine aid.
terra: Those who migrate and are then killed or die are promised good provision from God, so either form of death fails to cut the journey's return.
terra: God admits those migrants to an entrance pleasing to them, completing the promised provision of 22:58 after their death.
terra: The Prophet is asked whether he seeks payment, then told that his Lord's payment is better and that He is the best provider, locating the superior wage wholly with God.
terra: When death comes, the dying person asks to be returned, identifying death as the point at which the earthly course of action is cut.
terra: The request is to return and do righteous work, but a barrier remains until resurrection; work can no longer be resumed although its judgment and return remain ahead.
terra: God rewards them by the best they did, adds from His bounty, and provides without reckoning; the ayah makes the wage both “best” and more than a finite equivalence.
terra: The Prophet is told to contrast the punishment with the Garden of Eternity, which is a reward and destination for the mindful.
terra: The Garden's people have whatever they wish while remaining there, and the lasting gift is a promise for which God is answerable.
terra: The Prophet asks no wage except that whoever wills should take a path to the Lord, turning the supposed payment into benefit for the hearer.
terra: Noah asks his people for no wage because his wage rests only with the Lord of the worlds, freeing his hearers from human indebtedness.
terra: Hud repeats that he asks no wage and that his wage belongs only with the Lord of the worlds.
terra: Salih repeats the same refusal of human payment and places his wage only with the Lord of the worlds.
terra: Lot repeats the prophetic stance of seeking no wage from his people and receiving it only from the Lord of the worlds.
terra: Shuayb repeats the same formula, making service without a reproachful human claim a shared prophetic stance.
terra: God wills to confer favor on the oppressed and make them leaders and inheritors; divine menn here lifts a burden instead of laying one on the receiver.
terra: Worldly gifts are temporary enjoyment and adornment, whereas what is with God is better and more enduring; this is a direct passing-versus-remaining account of return.
terra: Those who believe and do righteous deeds are promised recompense by أَحْسَنَ الَّذِي كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ, the same transfer from good work to best return.
terra: Abraham is given his reward in this world and is among the righteous in the Hereafter, directly illustrating recompense returning in both domains.
terra: Believers who do righteous deeds are lodged in Garden chambers to remain there, explicitly calling that abiding destination the excellent reward of workers.
terra: A gift made to increase through people's wealth does not increase with God, while alms seeking God's face are multiplied; motive determines whether giving truly returns an increase.
luna: The section moves from the best human form to the lowest; this verse traces a person's weakness to strength and back to weakness and gray age, giving that reversal a bodily sequence.
terra: Even a mustard-seed weight hidden in a rock or anywhere in creation is brought forth by God, a concrete image of no deed becoming inaccessible to recompense.
terra: The Prophet says that any wage he might have asked is for the hearers themselves and that his own wage rests only with God, removing human debt from his service.
luna: The section's reward cannot be cut off; here those who recite, pray, and spend hope in a trade لن تبور, a transaction that will not perish, giving a concrete parallel for an enduring return.

luna: Completing 35:29's nonperishing trade, this verse says God will pay their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty, directly extending the section's uncut recompense. | terra: God pays the reciters and givers their wages in full and increases them from His bounty, explicitly replacing diminution with surplus.

luna: The section's B001 fatigue sense of م ن ن is a wearied traveler cut off from movement; here the eternal home granted by God's bounty has no نصب or لغوب, removing both fatigue and weariness from the lasting abode. | terra: The people settled in the lasting abode say that no weariness touches them there; the reward cannot leave its traveler stranded through the fatigue developed in the section.
terra: God revives the dead and records what people sent ahead as well as the traces they left, so death does not erase the intentional work whose return awaits.
terra: The townspeople are told to follow messengers who ask no wage and are rightly guided, making freedom from demanded repayment a sign of trustworthy guidance.
terra: On that day no soul is wronged and people are recompensed only for what they did, joining action to an exact return beyond death.
luna: The section moves from humanity's best form to a downward line; this verse says long life can reverse a person in creation, ننكسه في الخلق, giving that decline a direct bodily formulation.
terra: A person within the Garden asks whether they will die, introducing the precise mortality question raised by the section's menūn image.
terra: The answer excludes every death after the first and excludes punishment, making the rewarded life immune to the event that cuts earthly duration.
terra: God says He conferred favor upon Moses and Aaron, introducing the rescue and victory that follow as beneficent menn.
terra: Solomon is told هَذَا عَطَاؤُنَا فَامْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ; the positive bestowing sense of the named root stands beside a gift without reckoning.
terra: God calls the blessed provision His رزق and says مَا لَهُ مِن نَّفَادٍ, explicitly denying depletion.
terra: The Prophet asks no wage for the message and disclaims artificial pretension, keeping his work free of an obligation imposed on hearers.

luna: The section denies that reward is cut or reduced; this verse promises the patient a reward without account, adding the distinct idea of a return beyond ordinary reckoning. | terra: The patient are paid their reward بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ, another direct formulation of recompense not bounded by a diminishing measure.
terra: The Prophet and his opponents will die; this explicit shared mortality limits earthly life while leaving the separately promised uncut wage beyond that boundary.
terra: God removes the worst of their deeds and pays أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ الَّذِي كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ, a direct recurrence of the best deed becoming the measure of reward.
terra: Every soul is paid in full for what it did, and God's complete knowledge prevents any work from being lost in the reckoning.
terra: The Garden's inheritors settle wherever they wish and call it the excellent reward of workers, placing enduring freedom inside the work's returned wage.
terra: Immediately before 40:40 promises believing workers provision without reckoning, the believer contrasts this world's brief enjoyment with the Hereafter as the lasting abode.
terra: A believer who does righteous work enters the Garden and is provided for بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ, making the return to intentional action inexhaustible rather than merely equivalent.

luna: The section's B001 root م ن ن names a reward that is not cut or reduced; 41:8 gives the same promise, لهم أجر غير ممنون, to believers who do good. | terra: This is the same promise without an exception clause: faith and righteous action receive أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ, directly confirming that the recompense is neither cut nor reduced.
terra: The one who seeks the harvest of the Hereafter receives increase in it, while the seeker of the worldly harvest receives some of it but has no share in the Hereafter.
terra: Whoever earns a good deed receives an increase in its goodness; the حسن root here names a return that grows rather than being reduced.
terra: What people receive is temporary worldly enjoyment, while what is with God is better and more enduring for believers who trust Him.
terra: The blessed taste no death beyond the first death and are protected from torment, directly denying death any second power to terminate their reward.
terra: Creation in truth leads to each soul being recompensed for what it earned without injustice, linking created order to undiminished return.
terra: God accepts the best of these believers' deeds and overlooks their evils among the people of the Garden, turning أحسن action into an accepted otherworldly outcome.
terra: People have ranks according to what they did, and God fully repays their works without wronging them, an explicit non-diminished wage for action.
terra: Those killed in God's path do not have their deeds allowed to go astray, so death cannot erase the work whose result God preserves.

luna: The section's B003 sense of م ن ن as claiming a favor appears when Bedouins boast their submission to the Prophet; the reply assigns the favor of guidance to God rather than the recipients of the boast. | terra: The Bedouins count Islam as a favor to the Prophet, but the same ayah reverses the claim: God is the one who favored them by guiding them to faith.
terra: The rewarded are told to enter the Garden in peace on the Day of Eternity, explicitly naming the duration into which they enter.
terra: They have whatever they wish there and God has still more, completing 50:34 with provision that exceeds a closed measure.
luna: The section says the promised reward is not diminished; in this verse God joins believing descendants to their families without depriving the believers of anything from their deeds.
terra: The people of the Garden say God favored them and protected them from the scorching torment, joining positive menn to an otherworldly gift preserved from loss.
terra: Immediately before people await the Prophet's menūn in 52:30, he is told that by his Lord's favor he is neither soothsayer nor mad; divine favor sustains the one whose death they await.

luna: The section's B001 dictionary sense of المنون is death that cuts a life short; the disbelievers wait for the Prophet to be struck by ريب المنون, the opposite of the uncut reward promised him in 68:3. | terra: The unbelievers wait for رَيْبَ الْمَنُونِ to overtake the Prophet; their hope that death will cut his life stands against God's promise of an uncut reward to him in 68:3.
terra: The opponents are asked whether the Prophet demands a wage that leaves them burdened by debt, precisely contrasting an oppressive human payment with his God-given reward.
terra: God recompenses those who do good with الْحُسْنَى, directly joining beautiful action to the most beautiful return.

luna: The section's dictionary definition makes أجر what returns for a deed; this passage begins that sequence by saying a person has only what he strives for, connecting the recompense to his own effort. | terra: A human being has only what he intentionally strives for, grounding the section's definition of عمل in purposeful exertion.

luna: Continuing 53:39's account of striving, this verse says the effort will be seen; it gives the deed a recognized place before the recompense in 53:41. | terra: The striving named in 53:39 will be seen, so the deed does not vanish when its earthly performance ends.

luna: This verse completes 53:39-40 by saying the striving is then repaid with the fullest recompense, a direct formulation of the section's deed returning as reward. | terra: The striving is then recompensed with the fullest recompense; this ayah supplies the returning wage completed by 53:39-40.
terra: This ayah supplies the abundant fruit whose supply 56:33 then declares neither cut off nor withheld.
terra: Paradisal fruit is لَا مَقْطُوعَةٍ وَلَا مَمْنُوعَةٍ, neither cut off nor withheld, turning the section's cutting sense into a concrete provision scene.
terra: Charitable men and women who offer God a good loan have it multiplied and receive a noble reward, so purposeful giving returns enlarged.
terra: God created death and life to test who is أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا; death, the section's cutter of a lifetime, is placed inside the trial of best action rather than made the end of its value.
terra: By the Lord's favor the Prophet is not mad; this positive grace directly precedes his uncut wage in 68:3 and parallels the wording of 52:29-30.

luna: The section reads غير ممنون as an uncut reward; here the Prophet himself is promised أجر غير ممنون, making the same assurance personal to him. | terra: God promises the Prophet أَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ; the section explicitly sets this personal promise beside the identical reward promised to faithful workers.

terra: Within the same surah that promises the Prophet an uncut wage, his opponents are asked whether his requested wage has burdened them with debt; the answer separates divine reward from human obligation.

luna: The section cites this surah's exception pattern: 70:19 describes humanity as created anxious, and the following verses define the worshippers excepted from that condition. | terra: Humanity is described as created anxiously unstable, establishing another general human condition later interrupted by an exception.

luna: The section invokes the exception pattern; إِلَّا ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ begins the answer to 70:19's general human condition, as 95:6 sets believers and doers apart from the descent in 95:5. | terra: إِلَّا الْمُصَلِّينَ breaks the general condition of 70:19 with the same exception movement that breaks the descent in 95:6.

luna: This verse specifies the excepted worshippers as constant in prayer, showing a sustained practice behind the section's emphasis on intentional good deeds. | terra: Those excepted from human instability in 70:22 are constant in prayer, giving the exception an act characterized by continuity.

luna: Among the traits of those excepted in 70:22, this verse calls wealth a known right; treating it as a due rather than a favor claimed from someone clarifies the section's reading of a reward free of burdensome minnah.
luna: This verse names the recipients of the known right in 70:24, the asker and deprived; it completes that giving scene and distinguishes a due from a favor that can be held over them.

luna: The section says belief in the Day of Judgment is the precise opposite of 95:7's challenge; 70:26 names those who يصدقون بيوم الدين, making that contrast explicit. | terra: Those within the exception affirm the Day of Recompense, directly opposing the denial questioned in 95:7 and explaining why their work can carry beyond death.
terra: The long description of those excepted from 70:19 ends with their being honored in Gardens, supplying the lasting outcome of the exception.
terra: One who believes in the Lord fears neither بَخْسًا, shortchanging, nor رَهَقًا, an oppressive burden; both clauses clarify a reward that is unreduced and does not weigh upon its receiver.
terra: The Prophet is commanded وَلَا تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ, forbidding a gift or favor made to obtain more; his own uncut wage therefore cannot be a human favor that exacts a larger return.

luna: The section hears “not burdened by minnah” as a payment that makes no claim on its recipient; the righteous here say they feed others seeking God's face and want no reward or thanks from them. | terra: The righteous feed others while wanting no recompense and no thanks from them, freeing recipients from the debt and pressure associated with reproachful giving.
terra: God rewards those givers for patience with Garden and silk; the return comes from God after 76:9 explicitly refuses payment from the human recipient.
luna: The section ends by challenging denial of recompense; 82:6 similarly asks what has deceived the human being about his generous Lord, setting up the creation and denial sequence in 82:7-9.

luna: The section names خ ل ق in the claim that God created humanity in the best form; 82:7 says God created, proportioned, and balanced the human, a close creation scene before 82:9's denial of judgment.
luna: This verse continues 82:7's account of the fashioned human by saying God composed him in whatever form He willed, extending the creation scene tied to the section's 95:4.
luna: After 82:7-8 describe the fashioned human, this verse says بل تكذبون بالدين; that sequence joins the section's best-form creation in 95:4 to its challenge about denying the Judgment in 95:7.

luna: The section describes fatigue as stopping a traveler on the way; 84:6 instead pictures a person كادح إلى ربه and then meeting Him, carrying effort through to encounter. | terra: Humanity toils toward its Lord and will meet Him; the strenuous journey supplies the road on which the section contrasts fatigue that stops with reward that does not.

luna: The section cites 84:6's labor toward meeting the Lord; the next scene begins with the person's record placed in the right hand, showing how that meeting proceeds for one whose account is favorable.
luna: After 84:6's striving and meeting, this verse promises an easy reckoning; it gives the encounter a concrete outcome alongside the section's promised recompense.
luna: This verse completes the favorable meeting sequence after 84:6: the person returns to his people joyfully, a lived outcome of the easy account in 84:8.

luna: This verse identifies the disbelievers as deniers before 84:24's warning and 84:25's exception; its own contribution is the opposing stance to the believing group whose uncut reward the section cites.

luna: This verse's warning of painful punishment is the side of the boundary that 84:25 immediately excepts; its own contribution is to make the succeeding uncut reward a real exception. | terra: This ayah supplies the painful punishment immediately before 84:25's word-for-word exception, so the exception's rescue from the preceding outcome remains visible.

luna: The section's B001 dictionary reading of م ن ن as cutting or diminution is denied by غير ممنون here; 84:25 repeats the believing-doer exception after 84:24's warning of painful punishment. | terra: This repeats 95:6 almost verbatim: believers who do righteous deeds have أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ, placing the uncut reward after the surah's scene of toil toward the Lord and judgment.
terra: Believers who do righteous deeds receive Gardens with rivers beneath, and the ayah names this the great attainment rather than a reward that can be cut short.

luna: The section contrasts a worldly return with an afterlife share; this verse names people who prefer الحياة الدنيا, setting up the next verse's more lasting Hereafter. | terra: People prefer the nearer life, naming the choice of the perishing domain over the reward beyond it.

luna: This verse completes the contrast in 87:16 by calling the Hereafter خير وأبقى, a specific statement of the lasting value that helps explain the section's uncut reward. | terra: The Hereafter is better and more enduring, providing the explicit opposite to the preference stated in 87:16.
terra: The Godfearing person gives wealth to purify himself, staging intentional good work without exploiting its recipient.
terra: No one has a favor with him that must be repaid; this expressly removes the interpersonal debt carried by the section's burdensome menn.
terra: The giving seeks only the face of the Most High Lord, locating the act's purpose beyond human repayment.
terra: The giver will ultimately be satisfied, completing 92:18-20 with a divine return rather than a demanded human one.
terra: Believers who perform righteous deeds are named the best of creatures, directly joining the faith-and-work exception to a transformed human standing.
terra: Their reward with their Lord is everlasting Gardens in which they remain forever, making the return to 98:7's work explicitly unending.
terra: Whoever does an atom's weight of good sees it, making even the smallest intentional good return rather than disappear.
terra: Whoever does an atom's weight of evil sees it, marking the exact boundary that confirms deeds of either kind survive to their return.

luna: The section says the descending line and exception recur in this surah; 103:2 states that humanity is in loss, while 103:3 supplies the exception, paralleling the section's mortal decline and saved group. | terra: Humanity is placed in loss, matching the downward general line from which 95:6 makes its exception.

luna: The section points to the exception after decline; 103:3 repeats إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ, then adds mutual counsel in truth and patience to the spared group. | terra: Faith and righteous action open the same exception from 103:2's universal loss, with mutual truth and patience specifying the life that escapes it.
